B.Choice: Shift `text(every digit)` `text(five)` places to the right because `10^5` is multiplying by `text(10 five)` times.

Content: A rectangular prism made from unit cubes is shown.
problems/WI24G5M/media/3a.jpg
What is the volume, in `text(cubic units)`, of the rectangular prism?

Key.Rationale: The student adds `3` and `4`, which are the dimensions of the front of the prism.
The student counts only the front of the prism, forgetting to add the back of the prism.

`text(One)` way to count the cubes is to see the rectangular prism as a front and a back. The front is `3` cubes by `4` cubes, for a total of `12` cubes. The back has the same number of cubes, so `12+12` equals `24`.

Content: Which situation can be represented by the expression `1/5-:3`?

A.Choice: A board is `text(3 feet)` long. The board is cut into `5` equal pieces.

Key.Rationale: The student reverses the dividend and divisor.

B.Choice: A block of metal weighs `text(5 pounds)`. The block is divided into `3` equal pieces.

Key.Rationale: The student uses the reciprocal of `1/5`, then divides by `3`.

C.Choice: A bottle contains `1/5` `text(liter)` of water. The water is poured equally into `3` containers.

Key.Rationale: Pouring a fixed amount of water equally into `3` containers can be represented by a division expression.

D.Choice: A running track is `1/5` `text(kilometer)` in length. A runner runs the length of the track `3` times.

Key.Rationale: The student misinterprets a multiplication situation as a division situation.

Content: A crate will be filled with small cubes. The crate has a length of `text(4 feet)`, a width of `text(3 feet)`, and a height of `text(2 feet)`. `text(Each small cube)` has a side length of `text(1 foot)`. Which set of small cubes will completely fill the crate?

A.Choice: `2` layers of cubes with `12` cubes in `text(each layer)`

Key.Rationale: The height of the crate can be thought of as `2` layers. `text(Each layer)` would have `4xx3=12` cubes.

B.Choice: `4` layers of cubes with `5` cubes in `text(each layer)`

Key.Rationale: The student uses the length of the crate, `4`, as the number of layers, but incorrectly adds `3` and `2` to get `5` cubes for `text(each layer)`.

C.Choice: `6` layers of cubes with `12` cubes in `text(each layer)`

Key.Rationale: The student multiplies `2` by `3` to get `6` layers and then multiplies `4` by `3` to get `12` cubes in `text(each layer)`.

D.Choice: `12` layers of cubes with `5` cubes in `text(each layer)`

Key.Rationale: The student multiplies `4` by `3` to get `12` layers and then adds `3` and `2` to get `5` cubes in `text(each layer)`.

Content: Which statement is true?

A.Choice: A rhombus is always a square.

Key.Rationale: The student recognizes that both polygons would have `text(four)` equal sides, but that does not mean all rhombuses are squares.

B.Choice: A rectangle is always a rhombus.

Key.Rationale: The student recognizes that both polygons have `text(four)` sides but forgets that rectangles must have `text(four)` right angles.

C.Choice: A square is always a quadrilateral.

Key.Rationale: All squares have `text(four)` sides, which makes them quadrilaterals.

D.Choice: A parallelogram is always a rectangle.

Key.Rationale: The student reverses the connection between rectangles and parallelograms.

Content: Stan participated in a long jump contest. His `text(first)` jump was `5.96` `bbtext(meters)`. His `text(second)` jump was `9` `bbtext(centimeters)` farther than his `text(first)` jump. How far, in `bbtext(meters)`, was Stan’s `text(second)` jump?

Key.Rationale: The student converts `text(9 cm)` to `text(0.009 m)`.
There are `text(100 cm)` in `text(1 m)`, so to convert `text(9 cm)` to `text(meters)`, the student can divide `9` by `100` to get `0.09`. The sum of `0.09` and `5.96` is `6.05`.
The student converts `text(9 cm)` to `text(0.9 m)`.

Content: Jeremy bought `10` packages of rice. The amount of rice in `text(each package)` was the same. The total amount of rice was greater than `text(10 cups)`. For `text(each amount)` in the table, in `text(cups)`, determine whether it could be or could not be the amount of rice in `1` package.
Andre is running in a relay race on a team with `3` other people.

:ibox:• Andre runs his part of the race in `text(12.46 seconds)`.
• Each of the other runners completes a part in a time a little faster than Andre.
Which number is the `bbtext(best)` estimate of the total amount of time, in `text(seconds)`, it takes Andre’s team to complete the race?

Key.Rationale: The student rounds Andre’s time and does not add the rest of the team’s times.
The student rounds Andre’s time and then multiplies by `3`, not realizing there are `4` people total.
